A: Settings-as-sliders is less instantly recognisable as 'settings' than a gear (reads closer to filters/tune), and its stated justification (gear teeth alias at 16px) is empirically disproved by B's clean 16px gear.
1.75px stroke reads slightly light at 16px next to UI text compared with a 2px system.
Preview relies on an inlined copy of the symbols rather than referencing icons.svg (explained and mitigated in DECISIONS, but still a dual-source risk).
B: Alert triangle is optically undersized: path spans ~14.1 units wide vs the gear's ~17.9 and the cube's 16, visibly smaller than every sibling at 16/24/48px despite DECISIONS claiming a keystone system.
Alert exclamation dot and stem sit tight inside the small triangle at 16px; interior begins to clog where A's stays open.
Corner language slightly mixed: r=2 arcs on frames but cube/gear vertices rely on round joins only, so they read sharper than the bracket corners.
Preview page chrome does not adapt to prefers-color-scheme (panels cover both themes, but the page itself is light-only); same inlined-copy dual-source risk as A.

notes: Both are strong, verified, well-documented systems and tie on technical quality. The decisive difference is optical balance: A's pointed shapes overshoot per its stated rule and the six glyphs read as one evenly weighted family, while B's alert triangle is clearly undersized against its gear and cube at every rendered size, breaking family consistency on the brief's core demand. B counters with a genuinely 16px-legible scripted gear and richer sheet-level accessibility markup, which narrows but does not close the gap.
